subject: Residency assertion and hot-failover routing clarifications
messages:
From: Diana Morales <security@acme-analytics.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: legal@acme-analytics.com (James Li)
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Residency assertion and hot-failover routing clarifications

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the demo last week. Before we move forward with procurement we need a few clarifications about region pinning and your hot-failover behavior for data routed to the Redwood runtime. Our security and legal teams have the following asks:

1) Residency assertion: Can Redwood provide a written assertion (or DPA extract) that customer data for our tenant will remain in the US primary region for normal processing? We understand temporary exceptions are sometimes necessary for availability — we need the bounds of those exceptions.

2) Hot-failover policy: If there is an incident that impacts the US region, will Redwood route traffic to EU/APAC as a temporary failover? If so, under what conditions, for how long, and what notification cadence will you provide? We need to know if failover happens automatically or requires manual approval.

3) Controls during cross-border processing: If cross-region processing occurs, what controls apply to (a) KMS keys and encryption, (b) access to logs/trace data, and (c) any cached prompts/KV state?

4) Subprocessors & subprocessors’ locations: We need the current list of subprocessors with region mapping and an assurance on how you notify customers of additions.

5) Contract language & delivery: Please provide sample DPA wording (or an amendment) we can present to procurement that captures: region pinning, permitted failover windows, notification commitments, and data-at-rest/key handling during failover.

Can you also attach any simple architecture diagram that shows routing and how hot-failover would work?

We’d like to have the amendment signed by 2026-05-25 if possible. Happy to jump on a 30m call this week to walk through.

Thanks,
Diana Morales
Head of Security, Acme Analytics

Hi Diana —

Thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below; I’ve attached a one-page residency assertion and a draft DPA extract for procurement review (residency-assertion-template.docx / dpa-extract.txt). Nikhil and Monica are looped in for technical and compliance details.

Summary (short):
- Residency: We support region pinning at the tenant level. For normal traffic, data and inference compute remain in the pinned region (US) and we will not route requests out of region.
- Hot-failover: We support an emergency failover to a secondary region (EU or APAC) only under well-defined incident categories (regional infrastructure outage or critical degradation impacting >X% of requests). Failover is configured as automatic fallback by default but can be changed to manual by contract for customers that require explicit approval.
- Duration & notification: Temporary cross-region routing is intended as a short-term mitigation. Our standard commitment: notify security/contact within 4 hours of initiation and provide a written incident summary within 24 hours. Failover is reversed as soon as capacity stabilizes; typical max window we operate under for hot failover is 72 hours unless otherwise agreed.
- Controls during failover: Data remains encrypted in transit and at rest. Customer-managed KMS is supported (BYOK) — keys remain in the customer’s chosen region where supported; when customer-managed keys are not configured, we use tenant-isolated keys in our key-management system and log key usage. Access to logs/traces is restricted and flagged as part of the incident; we can provide filtered logs for audit. KV/prefix caches are invalidated after failover and rehydration happens in-region once traffic returns.
- Subprocessors: We maintain a current list and provide 30-day notice for additions for customers with contract protections.

Next steps I propose:
1) Please review the attached DPA extract and residency assertion.
2) If the language looks acceptable, James/legal can propose edits and we can produce a DocuSign amendment for signature.
3) Nikhil can share an architecture diagram (attached) and the operational runbook sections relevant to failover.

I attached: residency-assertion-template.docx and redwood-region-routing-diagram.png.

If you prefer, we can schedule a technical call Thursday or Friday — what time works for you?

Best,

Diana — quick technical supplement (short bullets + references):

- Failover triggers: health checks (P95 latency > 2x SLA threshold), availability zone + regional fabric incidents, or manual operator trigger for capacity exhaustion.
- Routing behavior: requests are routed via our smart router by tenant-id. When failover mode is active, routing policy marks the tenant as "failover-eligible" and only routes to pre-approved secondary regions. We do not arbitrarily broadcast to all regions.
- KMS and keys:
  - BYOK: recommended for customers who want cryptographic guarantee that key material never leaves their control. We support external KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, HSM).
  - Default: tenant-specific envelope keys stored in our KMS; usage logs are retained and can be exported.
- Logs/trace handling: PII is redacted from request logs by default; raw request bodies are not included in long-term log stores unless explicitly configured for debugging with customer consent. During failover, we tag all log entries with a failover flag and can export a scoped bundle for audits.
- Cache/kv: cached KV is ephemeral; we invalidate local caches on failover and do a controlled warm-up back in-region. This avoids stale context crossing regions.

Attachment: redwood-region-routing-diagram.png (attached) — the diagram shows the router, tenant-affinity table, and failover flip logic.

If you want, I can extract the exact contract language for the technical bits and hand it to legal for insertion.

-Nikhil
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Diana and team —

Following up with the items you requested:

- DocuSign amendment: https://www.docusign.com/example/Acme-Amendment-4821 — I populated the residency-and-failover clause in Section 2. Attached is a plain-text extract as well (dpa-extract.txt).
- Subprocessor list: public registry link (we maintain a live list) — https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-region-routing (see file: subprocessors_current_20260521.csv). We’ll provide formal 30-day notice for additions under the proposed amendment.
- SOC 2: We are SOC 2 Type II compliant — report access is available under NDA.

We can make the amendment require manual approval for any cross-region failover if Acme needs that stricter control; the tradeoff is a longer RTO in case of regional outages. Suggested language is in the draft (Section 2.1b) which says: "Hot-failover to a secondary region will be performed only upon manual approval by Redwood and written confirmation from Acme’s security contact, unless Redwood reasonably determines that immediate automated failover is required to preserve availability for critical customer traffic."

Please confirm whether Acme wants automated or manual failover in the amendment and whether the 72-hour default max window is acceptable. If yes, I’ll route the DocuSign request to James/legal and target signature by 2026-05-25.
